interpretations.plain_english_summary: This was House passage of the HALT Fentanyl Act. The bill would permanently place fentanyl-related substances as a class into Schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act and set penalties using the same quantity thresholds as fentanyl analogues.
interpretations.yea_meaning: A Yea vote supported passing the bill to permanently schedule fentanyl-related substances and apply the bill's penalty and research-registration changes.
interpretations.nay_meaning: A Nay vote opposed passing the bill to permanently schedule fentanyl-related substances and apply the bill's penalty and research-registration changes.
interpretations.policy_effect: The bill would move fentanyl-related substances from temporary classwide scheduling to permanent Schedule I status, apply fentanyl-analogue quantity thresholds and penalties, and create or revise registration paths for certain Schedule I research.
interpretations.interpretation_reason: Official roll-call wording identifies passage of the HALT Fentanyl Act, and the Congress.gov summary describes the scheduling, penalty, and research-registration changes.

interpretations.plain_english_summary: This was House passage of the Federal Law Enforcement Officer Service Weapon Purchase Act. The bill would direct the General Services Administration to create a program letting federal law enforcement officers buy retired firearms from the agencies that issued those firearms.
interpretations.yea_meaning: A Yea vote supported passing the bill to create the retired-service-weapon purchase program for federal law enforcement officers.
interpretations.nay_meaning: A Nay vote opposed passing the bill to create the retired-service-weapon purchase program for federal law enforcement officers.
interpretations.policy_effect: The bill would require GSA to establish a process for federal law enforcement officers to purchase retired agency-issued firearms from their issuing agencies.
interpretations.interpretation_reason: Official roll-call wording identifies passage of the bill, and the Congress.gov summary describes the GSA purchase-program requirement.

interpretations.plain_english_summary: This was House passage of the Improving Law Enforcement Officer Safety and Wellness Through Data Act. The bill would require the Department of Justice to report on targeted attacks on law enforcement officers, crime-reporting feasibility, and officer mental health resources.
interpretations.yea_meaning: A Yea vote supported passing the bill to require the DOJ reporting on officer attacks, crime-reporting systems, and mental health resources.
interpretations.nay_meaning: A Nay vote opposed passing the bill to require the DOJ reporting on officer attacks, crime-reporting systems, and mental health resources.
interpretations.policy_effect: The bill would create a DOJ reporting requirement rather than directly changing criminal penalties or law enforcement operations.
interpretations.interpretation_reason: Official roll-call wording identifies passage of the bill, and the Congress.gov summary describes the specific DOJ reporting requirement.

interpretations.plain_english_summary: This was House passage of the District of Columbia Policing Protection Act. The bill would repeal D.C. restrictions on police vehicular pursuits and generally require pursuits when no other means of apprehension is available, subject to listed exceptions.
interpretations.yea_meaning: A Yea vote supported passing the bill to repeal D.C. vehicular-pursuit restrictions and replace them with the bill's pursuit requirement and exceptions.
interpretations.nay_meaning: A Nay vote opposed passing the bill to repeal D.C. vehicular-pursuit restrictions and replace them with the bill's pursuit requirement and exceptions.
interpretations.policy_effect: The bill would change D.C. police-pursuit rules by removing the current restrictions described in the Congress.gov summary, adding a general pursuit requirement unless listed risk or effectiveness exceptions apply, and requiring a DOJ report on pursuit-alert technology.
interpretations.interpretation_reason: Official roll-call wording identifies passage of the bill, and the Congress.gov summary describes the D.C. vehicular-pursuit policy change and DOJ reporting requirement.

interpretations.plain_english_summary: This was House passage of the CLEAN DC Act. The bill would repeal D.C.'s Comprehensive Policing and Justice Reform Amendment Act of 2022 and restore or revive provisions changed by that act.
interpretations.yea_meaning: A Yea vote supported passing the bill to repeal D.C.'s 2022 policing and justice reform act and restore or revive provisions it changed.
interpretations.nay_meaning: A Nay vote opposed passing the bill to repeal D.C.'s 2022 policing and justice reform act and restore or revive provisions it changed.
interpretations.policy_effect: The bill would reverse D.C. policing reforms described in the Congress.gov summary, including provisions related to neck-restraint limits, body-worn camera procedures, and access to police disciplinary records.
interpretations.interpretation_reason: Official roll-call wording identifies passage of the bill, and the Congress.gov summary describes repeal of the D.C. policing and justice reform act and the provisions affected.
